##### Summary
Fixes  #8384
Fixes  #9730
##### Component Name
database
##### Test Plan

1. Make sure that `2 * 4096 * number-of-metrics-being-collected` bytes is more than the disk space quota. This should trigger the `Failed to flush dirty buffers quickly enough in dbengine instance` error message in the old code.
2. Make sure that a collector that has collected at least 34 minutes worth of metric data points stops collecting a specific metric (2 4K pages of metrics with 1 second collection interval). After a full database rotation you should start seeing the aforementioned error message.
pr_comments: I don't think that this looks like a fix, at best it seems to be a mitigation that hides the problem in the specific testing scenario that you have indicated. Why was the extra page pinned originally and what are we losing by disabling it?

> I don't think that this looks like a fix, at best it seems to be a mitigation that hides the problem in the specific testing scenario that you have indicated. Why was the extra page pinned originally and what are we losing by disabling it?

As discussed with @mfundul -- it's not as a fix but disabling a feature that doesn't work correctly. The pinning was done for performance reasons so that the active page and the previous (pinned one) are available in memory for queries (for a maximum of ~34 minutes worth of data)

Unpinning will result in the page being brought in back from the disk if we get an incoming query that needs to access that data (and the page is not available)

Given the headaches it causes I think its best to disable it (at least for now until we figure out how it can be improved / reworked).

Removing the pinned page should not reduce the performance in any scenario other than querying data that is between 34 and 17 minutes old on a system that is loaded heavily enough that those pages are not left in the cache. This seems reasonable as a trade for fixing the db-rotation to remove the flushing errors.

Please clean up the commit - it adds code that is not used. I can understand leaving the debug in as it may be useful again, but why the new function that is unused?

issue_context.title: using dbengine multihost results in connection/data loss to children as a result of "too slow disk"
issue_context.body:
<!--
When creating a bug report please:
- Verify first that your issue is not already reported on GitHub.
- Test if the latest release and master branch are affected too.
-->

##### Bug report summary
<!-- Provide a clear and concise description of the bug you're experiencing. -->
We have a Parent where 37 children are streaming around 3700 metrics each 2 seconds to parent. With the old dbengine setup per child everything is working fine. After upgrading to 1.24 and deleting the old db cache we now had problems and alerts lik "ipv4 tcphandshake last collected secs = 00:02:10 ago" for many children periodically after ~20 minutes. Looking into the dbengine netdata metrics revealed that the parent reported at the same time that the disk was to slow to write all metrics from the dbengin to disk. At the same time and during the time where data was not gather from children, netdata reported higher CPU usage.

My assumptions is now that before, each dbengin wrote to disk a different times smaller size of data and the disk was fast enough for netdata to write everything, and with the new single dbengine the data is now written at the same time which causes problems on netdata side.

To mitigate the data loss we reverted back to 1.23.2 on the parent. All children continue running on 1.24.0 (stable release channel)

comments:
May be related to https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/8384

Can you share your `var/log/netdata/error.log*` files? You may send them to me at markos@netdata.cloud if you don't want them to be public.

I looked into the nedata docker container:
```
bash-4.4# ls -al
total 8
drwxr-xr-x    2 netdata  root          4096 Jul 16 02:25 .
drwxr-xr-x    1 root     root          4096 Jul 16 02:25 ..
lrwxrwxrwx    1 root     root            11 Jul 16 02:25 access.log -> /dev/stdout
lrwxrwxrwx    1 root     root            11 Jul 16 02:25 debug.log -> /dev/stdout
lrwxrwxrwx    1 root     root            11 Jul 16 02:25 error.log -> /dev/stderr
bash-4.4# pwd
/var/log/netdata
```
and I don no longer have the docker logs as I restarted the container with the older version 1.23.2.

The container wires the logs to `stdout` so that the logging is handled by docker on the host instead of inside the container. You can then retrieve from docker using something like (assuming your container name):
```
docker logs netdata >error.log 2>&1
```
I updated the parent server to docker hubs `netdata:latest` and I can confirm that the problem no longer exists.
Good news. @mfundul will be happy to hear it when he returns next week.

review_comments: This code does not get called.

I know, I was experimenting with it when we discussed about timeouts and I left it there as a library function for future use. We have had other functions like that in the past, that we eventually used.
Do we still need this if pinning is disabled?

Not really but the idea was that we'll re-enable pinning as soon as possible, since Kosta has explicitly asked for it, so it's good to have a solution in-place. Since it affects disk space usage for users it's a good idea to let them get used to the new disk space calculation early on.

Moreover, it's a good idea that disk space is always bigger than cache space. It won't be pretty if the user only keeps 1% of the real time metrics because the disk space is 64MB but 1000 child nodes are streaming to it.

I think that we have to view re-enabling pinning as a piece of work to start from scratch. Pinned pages cannot prevent the rotation so there will need to be a rethink of how pinned pages work so that they can survive the cleanup and get moved to a later file / extent in the db.

Agreed, right now the problem is that we don't remember which collectors came and went, and we don't have a strict reference counting model for them. In theory, if rotation could pre-empt a collector's reference without causing a crash, we could re-enable pinning.
